description: Films with an allowed rental duration of 5 days or more are included; exactly 5 days counts.

b.request: Films with `rental_duration >= 5` are kept, grouped by `original_language_id` with NULL as its own group, and the output is one unrounded row: the unweighted mean of the per-group `AVG(rental_rate)` values, then the unweighted mean of the per-group `COUNT(*)` values (NULL if no groups remain).
b.sql: SELECT AVG(CAST(g.avg_rate AS DOUBLE)) AS mean_of_avg_rental_rate, AVG(CAST(g.films AS DOUBLE)) AS mean_of_group_counts FROM (SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY original_language_id) AS g;
b.raw: Films with `rental_duration >= 5` are kept, grouped by `original_language_id` with NULL as its own group, and the output is one unrounded row: the unweighted mean of the per-group `AVG(rental_rate)` values, then the unweighted mean of the per-group `COUNT(*)` values (NULL if no groups remain).

a.request: Considering only films whose allowed rental duration (`film.rental_duration`) is at least 5 days, group them by original language (`film.original_language_id`), treating films with no original language as one group of their own, and for each group work out the average rental rate (`rental_rate`) and the number of films. Then, across those groups, what is the average of the group average rental rates and the average of the group film counts? Treat each group equally, ignore missing values (missing if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_rate) AS avg_of_group_avg_rates, AVG(g.film_count) AS avg_of_group_counts FROM (SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY original_language_id) AS g;

d.request: For films with `rental_duration >= 5`, group by `original_language_id` (with NULL as its own group), compute each group's `AVG(rental_rate)` and `COUNT(*)`, then return the unrounded mean of the group averages and the unrounded mean of the group counts as one row, or NULL if no groups remain.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_rate) AS mean_of_group_avg_rates, AVG(g.cnt) AS mean_of_group_counts FROM (SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY original_language_id) AS g;

c.request: Using 5 days (`film.rental_duration`) as the cutoff for a long allowed rental period and considering only films with a long one, group them by original language (`film.original_language_id`), treating films with no original language as one group of their own, and for each group work out the average rental rate (`rental_rate`) and the number of films. Then, across those groups, what is the average of the group average rental rates and the average of the group film counts? Treat each group equally, ignore missing values (missing if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round. Films with an allowed rental duration of 5 days or more are included; exactly 5 days counts.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_rate) AS avg_of_group_avg_rates, AVG(g.films) AS avg_of_group_film_counts FROM (SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY original_language_id) AS g;
